articles.title: Revealed: How much direct-to-consumer revenue games publishers really made in Q3 2026
articles.text:
We analyse the D2C sales from the top public companies and see what they're saying about taking payments off-store

 By Craig Chapple 

 November 27, 2026 

 Share:

 Prefer PocketGamer.biz on Google 

 Date 
 Type 
 Companies Involved 
 Key Datapoint 

 Nov 27, 2026 
 report 
 
 Appcharge 
 AppMagic 
 DoubleDown Interactive 
 G5 Entertainment 
 Huuuge Games 
 Modern Times Group 
 Newzoo 
 Playstudios 
 Playtika 
 SciPlay 
 Sensor Tower 
 Stillfront Group 
 Take-Two Interactive 
 Ten Square Games 
 Zynga 
 
 D2C Tracker Q3 2026 

 Stay Informed 

 Get Industry News In Your Inbox…

 Sign Up Today

 This article was first published in the PocketGamer.biz newsletter. Subscribe for more content like this straight to your inbox here - you'll even get discounts on PGC events. 

 Now that the company financials are out for the last quarter, we’re taking a look again at the latest developments in the direct-to-consumer space and how publishers are performing.

 The last time we analysed D2C earnings, some publishers were still growing their share of off-store sales, while others had seemingly plateaued. So what happened in Q3?

 Playtika, MTG, Stillfront 

 For Playtika, which owns the likes of Disney Solitaire maker Superplay and June’s Journey developer Wooga, D2C revenue increased 31.4% year-over-year to $275.1 million in Q3, but decreased sequentially from the previous quarter by 4.1%. That means that, for the third quarter in a row, the company’s D2C sales declined.

 However, third-party platform revenue also declined sequentially for the third time, down 14.3% Y/Y. Company CFO Tae Lee said cost of revenue declined for the company, however, “mainly because platform fees fell as our D2C business grew”.

 Overall, D2C represented 40.8% share of total sales, which Lee said was a goal hit ahead of schedule. “D2C remains a core part of our strategy and we will continue to optimise across channels as the platform landscape evolves.”

 Looking forward, the Disney Solitaire web store was launched on November 18th, 2026, which could spark a rise for sales in the coming quarter as one of the company’s best-performing games.

 At Modern Times Group (MTG), which owns studios including Innogames, Plarium and Snowprint, D2C took a record 42% share of revenue in Q3, up from 38% in Q2 and 26% the year prior. Breaking that down, its midcore division Playamp saw D2C make up 55% of sales, compared to 41% from mobile app stores. A year prior in Q3 2025, D2C represented 33% of revenue, while app stores accounted for 62%. Playsimple reported 0% in D2C revenue.

 MTG president and CEO Maria Redin said that Google introduced new rules on alternative billing and began charging platform fees on external links for Android players in the US from October 1st, “reducing some of the cost advantages of D2C from these players”.

 Over at Stillfront, which owns the likes of Goodgame Studios and Babil Games, D2C bookings hit 47% of bookings. That puts it above 42% of bookings from third-party stores and 11% from ads. The company said the increase was driven mainly by web shops launched in more of its games, such as BitLife.

 Huuuge Games, G5 Entertainment, Ten Square Games 

 Huuuge Games saw D2C reach a new record share of 45.4% in Q3, up from 42.5% in Q2. The company claimed this share grew to approximately 48% in September and October 2026. As of November, Huuuge Games has moved its web store to its own platform, “which gives the company more control over the purchase experience”.

 To show the change in D2C - in the nine months ending September 30th, 2025, third-party platforms represented $136.9m in revenue, while D2C made up $40.1m. In the nine months ending September 30th, 2026, third-party platforms accounted for $90.8m in revenue, while D2C had risen to $68.4m. While a drop in overall revenue, D2C sales rose 70.7% Y/Y, accounting for a 43% share.

 The publisher said D2C remains a “strategic priority”.

 Elsewhere, G5 Entertainment recorded a 15.7% increase in G5 Store gross revenue Y/Y and 6.8% quarter-on-quarter in Q3. Direct processing of mobile player payments also continued to scale, reaching 21% ($1.8m) of mobile gross revenue, up from 17% in Q2. The company put a record gross margin of 74.1% primarily down to the accelerating shift toward direct checkout, the G5 Store and advertising.

 Ten Square Games said its D2C platform is being “systematically expanded across its products”. In September, D2C payments accounted for approximately 22% of group bookings. That was down from 23% in Augusted and 24% from May to July. Fishing Clash is the best performer, with 31% of bookings coming from D2C sales in September.

 The company is expanding this further with web stores for Trophy Hunter and Medal Hunter in the works.

 Ten Square Games also noted that for games covered by Google Play Level Up, the commission on purchases from existing players was reduced by an additional five percentage points. 

 “For purchases made by new players in selected markets, the total benefit compared with the previous commission level reaches 10 percentage points,” it said. “This is particularly relevant for the Group – after nine months of 2026, 44.8% of Ten Square Games’ bookings were processed through Google Play worldwide.”

 DoubleDown, SciPlay, Playstudios 

 Social casino firm DoubleDown Interactive said D2C revenue rose to $44.6m in Q3 2026, compared to $16.5m in Q3 2025, a rise of 170% Y/Y. These off-store sales accounted for 58% of social casino sales, up from 20.9% the year prior and 52.4% in the previous quarter.

 Another social casino developer, SciPlay, saw overall revenue decrease by 12% in Q3, owing to “ongoing softness of the broader social casino F2P market”. This was partially offset by D2C revenue growth, however, rising to 31% of sales at $53m, up 33% Y/Y. That compares to a revenue share of 20% the year prior and 29% in Q2.

 Playstudios reported $16m in D2C revenue in Q3, up 108% Y/Y. The company said these sales "represent an increasingly important component of the company's revenue mix, supporting improved platform economics and greater control over player relationships”.

 Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick once again referred to D2C sales in the publisher's mobile business during its Q2 2027 earnings call. He said while the company is not disclosing the percentage it takes of revenue, D2C sales are “significant” and growing. “It obviously has a very meaningful margin and bottom line impact. It also allows us to interact directly with our consumers to market to them directly, and that's positive as well.”

 D2C tracking and player spending estimate limitations 

 I wanted to close out this report with two things worth noting. Firstly, Sensor Tower says it has introduced Web Store Revenue estimates to its platform, along with an Ad Monetisation tool and IAP Insights, showing which offers are generating the most sales.

 I’ve mentioned a few times how there’s increasingly little visibility on how the overall mobile games market is truly performing. So hopefully this shines some light on how much money D2C is really making.

 Newzoo currently provides D2C estimates as part of its overall numbers, but doesn't break this down. Earlier this year, an Appcharge report said the D2C market for games could be worth $17 billion - a conservative estimate, according to CMO Gil Tov-ly.

 Sensor Tower SVP for gaming and entertainment Chirag Ambwani highlighted the disparity between store sales and D2C revenue at the State of Gaming Summit 2026 during Gamescom this year.

 He said while it has looked like Monopoly Go revenue is on the decline from App Store and Google Play estimates, web store sales are estimated to have grown substantially to around a third of its revenue.

 According to official figures, Scopely’s blockbuster surpassed $8 billion from player spending in the summer.

 We also just reported that, according to AppMagic (owned by Sensor Tower) data for October, Tencent Games sales declined by 11% . This stirred some conversation online, so I thought I’d look at official figures for the year.

 In Q3, domestic game revenue rose by 11% Y/Y to ¥47.6bn ($7.1bn), primarily driven by Delta Force, Valorant Mobile and Honor of Kings. International sales declined 9% Y/Y to ¥18.9bn ($2.8bn), which it pinned on high base sales for certain Supercell Games and the release of Dying Light: The Beast in Q3 2025.

 Valorant Mobile and Delta Force were said to have achieved lifetime high DAUs.

 Of course, Tencent’s gaming empire is vast and mobile isn’t broken down specifically. But its official figures and positive statements show that sales were in fact on the rise overall - perhaps owing to D2C sales, as well as revenue from its own storefronts and other Android platforms in China.

articles.title: Google’s $338m UK developer settlement opens for claims
articles.text:
By 
 
 Vikki Blake 

 / 24th November 2026 

 Any UK developer that has sold apps, games, subscriptions or in-app content through Google Play since August 2018 is now eligible for a share of a $338m (£260m) settlement with Google.

 More than 10,000 UK businesses are thought to be eligible, and developers can check their provisional award and claim for free through the official claims website . The claims period runs from today (November 24) until March 24, 2027.

 The settlement stems from a collective action brought by Professor Barry Rodger of Strathclyde University Law School, which alleged that Google’s Play Store commissions of up to 30% were excessive and broke competition law. Google settled without admitting liability, and the Competition Appeal Tribunal approved the deal on September 16, finding its terms just and reasonable.

 According to Rodger’s legal team, it’s the largest payout for members of a collective action the Tribunal has ever approved.

 Payments are based on Google’s records of each developer’s Play Store sales and the commission they paid between August 22, 2018 and July 31, 2026. Developers whose apps made $9,750 (£7,500) or less on the Play Store during that period are guaranteed a minimum of $260 (£200), even if their proportionate share would have been lower. The biggest developers could receive millions.

 Apps that were free to download are also eligible, as long as they sold subscriptions or in-app content and the developer didn’t opt out of the claim.

 As the case was brought on an opt-out basis, many eligible developers may not know about it. Invitations to claim have been emailed to the addresses linked to developers’ Google Play accounts, but those who haven’t received one can still check their eligibility on the claims website.

 “If an email about a Google settlement has landed in your inbox, it isn’t spam,” said Rodger. “After more than two years of work, compensation is now ready for the UK businesses that sold apps and digital content on the Google Play Store, from one-person studios working at their kitchen tables to established games companies.”

 Once the claims period closes, the Tribunal will review how the settlement is distributed before any payments are made.

 The case is separate from the collective claim brought by Liz Coll on behalf of UK consumers, which is currently going through trial.

This carries direct financial and compliance relevance for any operator with UK Google Play sales history.

articles.title: What 195 industry leaders think about player retention and engagement challenges
articles.text:
We dive into the data from ZBD's industry survey, with insights from CCO Gordon Thornton and Two and a Half Gamers' Jakub Remiar

 By Craig Chapple 

 November 26, 2026 

 Share:

 Prefer PocketGamer.biz on Google 

 Date 
 Type 
 Companies Involved 
 Key Datapoint 

 Nov 26, 2026 
 report 
 
 ZBD 
 
 Retention and re-engagement 

 Stay Informed 

 Get Industry News In Your Inbox…

 Sign Up Today

 Gaming and fintech firm ZBD conducted a survey of 195 games industry leaders earlier this year to research the challenges and trends for player retention and engagement in their games. 

 In exclusive new data provided to PocketGamer.biz, the survey showed that developers monetising primarily with IAPs reported less of a challenge in balancing their game’s monetisation strategies with the user experience. 36% reported this as a pain point for IAP games, compared to 53% for in-app advertising and 59% for hybrid monetisation.

 Early user drop-off was said to be a greater challenge with hybrid games (41%), compared to 32% for IAA and 24% for IAP games.

 The biggest challenges for all monetisation types was monetisation vs UX friction (51% aggregate) and retaining spenders (45%).

 Strategic impact 

 IAP games reported that community and social features have a higher impact on retention and engagement than other monetisation models. Notably, live ops features, promotions and events had a significantly higher effect on retention and engagement for IAA games than IAP and hybrid titles at 85%.

 Asked about that latter data point, ZBD chief commercial officer Gordon Thornton told PocketGamer.biz that the data simply reinforces the state of the industry and natural performance evolution.

 “IAP games have been building their player engagement strategies for over a decade," he said. "However, many are now starting to experience live ops performance fatigue, which is consistent with what we found in our original report. Alternatively, IAA games have only started leaning heavily into live ops in recent years, so they're likely reaping the initial benefit of fresh mechanics boosting player engagement.”

 Two and a Half Gamers’ Jakub Remiar commented: “Live ops events mainly drive revenue spikes for IAP games; no amount of live ops will save your game if retention is weak. 

 “On the other hand, IAA games usually have much less robust economies and metagame systems to begin with. So I can imagine it is fixing some of those shortfalls there, where it's also being positioned as a metagame feature, which would make sense if it drives retention.”

 Retention and engagement improvements 

 Asked which factors will drive the biggest improvements in retention and engagement over the next 12 to 24 months, IAA games (43%) rated real-money referrals as potentially the largest driver. That compared to 29% for IAP games and 25% for hybrid.

 Hybrid games (51%) rated stronger player personalisation as the most impactful potential for improvement, followed by better cross-team collaboration at 47%. By comparison, IAA games rated stronger player personalisation at 34% and better cross-team collaboration impact at 23%.

 IAP games noted that strong player personalisation and in-game rewards and loyalty systems would drive the biggest improvement. Live ops strategies were rated higher at 42% for IAP games than IAA (32%) and hybrid (34%).

 Remiar said personalisation and in-game rewards and loyalty systems were likely seen as the b biggest improvement rivers because games that already have a firm grip on how to monetise their player base are now heavily into the optimisation phase, where each tweak is able to squeeze more revenue per user.

 “Personalisation across all verticals, not just in-game, is supporting this. This is great for developers who are still growing (which is basically everyone) as they can focus on their users and keep them playing for longer. In-game rewards complement this directly.”

 On real-money referrals and why they are rated lower in IAP and hybrid games compared to IAA, Remiar said: “User quality differs drastically between IAP and IAA games, as does player motivation. In IAP games, players already have money; therefore, they don’t find real money referrals that attractive. IAA players, by contrast, are there for cheaper dollar-per-hour entertainment, so they find real-money referrals much more attractive.”

 Past performance 

 Industry leaders surveyed were asked whether their retention and re-engagement budget had increased, decreased or stayed the same over the past year.

 Hybrid (59%) and IAP (56%) developers said they saw their budgets increase over the prior 12 months. Meanwhile 60% of IAA developers said their budgets stayed the same, with 13% stating their budgets had decreased.

 The survey also reported that 2% of IAA developers have no dedicated retention budget.

 While over half of IAP developers are said to be increasing their budgets for retention and re-engagement, 44% aren’t. That’s despite the challenge of high and ever-increasing UA costs for new users, a point that Thornton highlights.

 “Chasing the same new users as everyone else and hoping they stick around to spend is getting increasingly expensive and delivering a lower ROI," he said.

 “On the flip side, investing in retaining existing users who have proven their worth can build a more sustainable active user base as a game’s lifecycle matures. Adding more context to the 44% data point: of the 44%, only 7% are decreasing budgets, while the rest are holding budgets steady.

 “Not every studio is going to be a first mover, and some may not feel the current headwinds as much as others, but I'd expect we'll see a continued shift toward more studios increasing retention budgets year over year."

 Learn about player retention, engagement, UA and more at Pocket Gamer Connects London on January 18th and 19th.

articles.title: Supercell offers Clash Royale players extra gold to encourage their return
articles.text:
Returning players can claim up to 49.6% extra gold as part of a limited-time event

 By Paige Cook 

 November 24, 2026 

 Share:

 Prefer PocketGamer.biz on Google 

 Supercell is incentivising its lapsed Clash Royale players to return by offering them interest on their existing gold balances.

 The amount of additional gold players can claim increased depending on how long they have been away.

 The event runs from November 24th to December 31st, 2026.

 Stay Informed 

 Get Industry News In Your Inbox…

 Sign Up Today

 Supercell has launched a new initiative to re-engage Clash Royale players by offering them interest on the in-game currency they may have left behind.

 Named The Royale Interest, this limited-time event lets returning players claim up to 49.6% additional gold, with the amount increasing the longer the player has been away from the game. 

 The event runs from November 24th to December 31st, with players able to claim their new gold balance simply by returning to the game. 

 Players can use the additional currency to upgrade cards, purchase new ones from the in-game shop and establish their own clans.

 Ten years on 

 The player reactivation initiative comes after Clash Royale celebrated its 10th anniversary this year , with the title having generated almost $5 billion in lifetime player spending as of March 2026. 

 Elsewhere, Supercell has been expanding the Clash Royale IP beyond mobile. Its tabletop game with Maestro Media, Clash Royale: The Grand Arena , reached its Kickstarter funding goal within an hour of launching its campaign.

articles.title: Data digest: Monopoly Go hits $8bn, Block Blast and Vita Mahjong lead ad charts, Korea stats, more
articles.text:
By 
 
 Vikki Blake 

 / 25th November 2026 

 Every Wednesday we break down the latest data, research and financial results into digestible chunks.

 Read on for the numbers you need to know about without the fluff.

 This column is sponsored by Xsolla , which can help you to create a seamless online store where web purchases can quickly generate new revenue – from launch to beyond. Get started here . 

 Monopoly Go passes $8bn in lifetime player spend 

 Monopoly Go has passed $8bn in lifetime player spending, pocketgamer.biz reports. Scopely told the outlet that the milestone was passed this summer, up from the $6bn the game hit in 2025, and just over three years after its April 2023 launch.

 AppMagic estimates make Monopoly Go the top grossing game on Google Play in 2026 so far, with more than $400m in net revenue since January. It has made $477m net on the App Store this year. Neither figure includes revenue from Scopely’s direct-to-consumer platform.

 Block Blast and Vita Mahjong lead ad creative charts 

 SocialPeta’s latest ad creative charts show Block Blast in front by the number of ad creatives in circulation on iOS, and a tighter race on Android, where Oakever Games / Learnings / Vita Studio dominates.

 The Chinese firm has claimed the top three spots on Android with Vita Mahjong, Amaze Go and Meowdoku. Block Blast is in fourth, and in fifth there’s another Oakever title, Tile Explorer.

 On iOS, Oakever / Vita / Learnings take up three of the top five with Amaze Go in second), Vita Mahjong in fourth and Meowdoku in fifth. SpinX’s Cash Club Casino is in third.

 Downloads drop but monetisation grows in maturing Korean market 

 Sensor Tower’s new report on the South Korean mobile game market suggests downloads are slowing but IAP revenue is still growing.

 It’s a sign that the market is maturing, says the data firm, which says downloads fell 38% from 540m in 2021 to 390m in 2026. IAP revenue has remained steady at around $5bn per year though – “this divergence signals a shift away from acquisition-led growth toward retention, re-engagement, live ops and more effective monetisation,” said Sensor Tower.

 Three key Korean publishers are also seeing the most growth outside their native market: MapleStory maker Nexon, Random Dice Defense publisher 111% and Pizza Ready creator Supercent.

 Colony Flow makes $13.7m in Q3 as flow puzzles take over 

 In 2026 alone, AppMagic has tracked more than 570 games using “pixel”, “flow” or “loop” in their store listings, and six of the top 10 hybridcasual puzzle games by IAP revenue in Q3 were flow puzzles built on a Pixel Flow-inspired core.

 Onesoft’s Colony Flow climbed more than 400 places to seventh, with $13.7m in IAP revenue and 9.5m installs. Rotatelab’s Cube Land, which takes the format into 3D, rounded off the top 10 with more than $9.9m and 4.8m installs, after revenue grew 1,226% quarter on quarter. Moon Active has also joined the trend with Jelly Busters.

 Tencent commits $140m to Golden Spatula 

 Tencent will invest $140m (CNY 1bn) over the next three years in Golden Spatula, its China-only mobile version of Riot Games’ Teamfight Tactics, according to Niko Partners . The money will be spread across product development, content creation, community engagement and esports.

 The game has more than 240m registered users and over 50m monthly active players, with a PC version planned. Tencent also announced a new annual championship with a $1.4m (CNY 10m) prize pool.

 Walking Zombie 2 passes 100m Google Play downloads 

 Alda Games’ Walking Zombie 2 has passed 100m downloads on Google Play, and more than 103m across mobile, the studio has announced . It’s only the second Czech mobile game to reach the milestone, after Madfinger Games’ Dead Trigger 2.

 The self-published game launched in 2018 and still brings in a million new players a month, with 99% of its players outside the Czech Republic. Alda says Walking Zombie 3 is on the way.

 Nexon reclaims Korea’s top spot with $881m Q3 

 Nexon was South Korea’s highest-earning games company in Q3, according to Niko Partners , with revenue of $881m (KRW 1.2312tn) and operating profit of $266m (KRW 371.8bn).

 Growth was driven by the MapleStory franchise, where revenue rose 72% year on year.

 Krafton, which led the Korean industry in the first half of the year, lost the top spot after its PC revenue fell 57% quarter on quarter.

articles.title: October 2026 mobile game charts: Top Lords takes off, Tencent falls 11% and AI listens in
articles.text:
A deep dive into the global mobile game rankings across the App Store and Google Play

 By Aaron Astle 

 November 24, 2026 

 Share:

 Prefer PocketGamer.biz on Google 

 Date 
 Type 
 Companies Involved 
 Key Datapoint 

 Nov 23, 2026 
 report 
 
 Bandai Namco 
 Capcom

 DeNA

 Garena

 King

 Miniclip 
 Mojang 
 Roblox 
 Scopely 
 Supercent 
 Tencent 
 The Pokemon Company 
 Voodoo 
 
 October 2026 game charts 

 Stay Informed 

 Get Industry News In Your Inbox…

 Sign Up Today

 Below you can see the latest top games and companies by downloads and revenue for October 2026, as well as the big stories and trends from the last month. Data is provided by AppMagic .

 Check out profiles of the world's top publishers in the Top 50 Mobile Game Makers 2026 list . Meet them in person at events like Pocket Gamer Connects London 2027 on January 18th and 19th.

 Note that these estimates of net revenue are from player spending across the App Store and Google Play only. It does not feature estimates from alternative marketplaces or direct-to-consumer platforms.

 TOP GROSSING MOBILE GAMES

 The big stories: SD Gundam G Generation Eternal’s autumnal comeback 

 SD Gundam G Generation Eternal shot up 74 positions in the top grossing rankings this October, re-entering the top 100 and landing in 39th place. The Bandai Namco title made $10.9 million net during the month, up 117% compared to September and its best performance since April.

 Currently in its second year, the Gundam game is building a pattern of revenue surges during the spring and autumn. October 2025 was its second-best month last year, spiking after a decline through the summer.

 This October has done the same, though lands as Gundam Eternal’s third highest-grossing month of 2026 so far. The rise coincided with its 1.5-year anniversary with login events, featured units, free pulls and more.

 The big stories: Top Lords aims for the top 

 Top Lords shot onto the scene with a record month this October, generating $9m. This Game Spark title released quietly during the summer months, building to its first $1m in August and steamrolling into autumn.

 Player spending climbed by 174% month-over-month in September, hitting $4.5m, before growing by another 99% into October. Compared to industry competition, this moved Top Lords up the rankings by 80 places last month, from 136th to the 56th most lucrative mobile game.

 It’s a trend aligning with a growing install base, from around 1.5m total in August to nearly 10m as of October. Its Last War-esque gameplay sees players grow an army along the bottom of their screen to shoot down advancing enemies.

 Daily revenue has been growing steadily since June and peaked at $377,000 on October 30th. It’s continuing to grow in November.

 Other notable stories: 

 Pokémon Trading Card Game Pocket made $14m in player spending this October, far from its astronomic origins but still landing it in the top 30 among all mobile games. In fact, its position rose by 24 places compared to September, up into 27th place. This rise wasn’t exactly a record breaker, but did come alongside the limited-time Deluxe Pack Mega set.

 Wrapping up the game’s second year, this set of cards was made available for a few weeks with just four cards per pack instead of five. However, among them, players had the chance to find fan-favourite Mega Pokémon like Mega Rayquaza, Lucario, Blastoise and Blaziken. More than 400 cards were available in the pack, the most to date, likely sparking serious collectors to get spending.

 The month also ended with anniversary content and another new card set, Dual Fusion, which has introduced cards with two types for the first time in Pokémon TCG history. Mega Greninja is both Water and Darkness type, for example.

 Wuthering Waves also saw a small resurgence in October, bouncing back after a September lull. Monthly spending grew from $9.3m to $15.1m, up 62%, marking its best month since June. Daily spending peaked at the start of the month, immediately following the release of version 3.7 and new gacha character Hsin, a powerful Electro DPS unit. New weapons were also added, as was the new area Simulacrum Nexus of Mengzhou.

 Finally, Capcom’s new mobile-exclusive Monster Hunter Outlanders launched right at the tail end of the month. It didn’t have time to top global charts for October, but did pick up more than $3m in player spending within four days.

 The game has been developed by TiMi Studio Group with Garena serving as publisher in Southeast Asia, monetised in part through its gacha system. This allows players to take control of not only their own customisable hunter but other characters with their own weapons and elemental affinities too.

 The top grossing mobile games for October 2026 

 Honor of Kings spent yet another month at the top of the charts, being the only title to surpass $100m net during October. Tencent’s giant has held onto the top spot since January.

 Roblox ranked second with $94.3m, followed by Monopoly Go at $74.6m. Notably, the four highest-grossing games all held onto their positions from September, with Microfun’s Gossip Harbor just shy of third place at $74.1m. This was down from a silver-medal peak in August.

 Dream Games’ Royal Match surpassed Candy Crush for a place in the top five this October, pushing ahead at $62.8m. Royal Match’s earnings grew 1% M/M while Candy Crush’s fell almost 10%, ultimately making $56.1m last month.

 Whiteout Survival, Kingshot, Coin Master and Township rounded out the top 10, the latter two moving up from 11th and 14th respectively.

 Collectively, mobile games generated almost $3.5 billion in net revenue during the month. The figure was down 13% year-over-year and 2% compared to September.

 MOST DOWNLOADED MOBILE GAMES

 The big stories: The rise of Rotate Rings 

 Nebula Studio netted a big win this October with the soaring success of Rotate Rings. Up from 199th place in September’s free games charts to eighth in October, the meteoric rise saw daily downloads reach beyond 650,000 per day and almost 12.6m over the course of the month.

 As its name implies, the game tasks its millions of players with rotating interlocked rings , aiming to line up gaps.

 No other title in the top 10 achieved such a sudden surge up the rankings last month. Compared to 2.5m downloads in September, it meant a 404% M/M rise.

 The Singapore-based studio’s catalogue consists of more than 10 games, spearheaded by fellow puzzle title Mahjong Blast - Tile Puzzle Game. It’s a game with more than 100m downloads on the Play Store alone. Rotate Rings has already reached 14m installs on the Play Store, so whether or not it goes on to overtake the flagship, it’s certainly one to watch. It’s already the third most-downloaded mobile game in Nebula Studio’s portfolio.

 The big stories: Memes for millions 

 MemeMix Challenge: Funny Party arrived on the scene this September and really took off in October. From less than 200,000 downloads, it suddenly accelerated to 7.8m in October with its AI features evidently grabbing attention.

 Amobear VN Game Global designed this title as a test of players’ voices, with AI tech evaluating tone, pitch and rhythm as players aim to mimic sounds to earn points. It also includes sound packs like animal noises, superhero quotes and an ‘anime edition’. So far, daily installs peaked on October 4th at 393,000.

 Other notable stories: 

 Minecraft’s mobile version returned to the top 50 this October, landing in 37th place for downloads with more than 5.8m fresh installs.

 Among last month’s downloads, 4.9m of them came from Google Play, compared to just 929,000 from the App Store. The rise happened to occur during the latest test of King’s Minecraft Blast, where gamers in Canada and Australia got to try the spinoff for the first time.

 Still, it’s worth noting Minecraft’s downloads remained below their 2026 peak of 7.6m installs this April, even if they turned around September’s decline.

 Royal Kingdom also rose up the charts with its best month since June, earning 5.7m new installs and landing in 41st place. That was a big rise from 84th in September but couldn’t quite catch up to Royal Match in 30th.

 Meanwhile, Supercent’s Bulldozer Master overtook Royal Kingdom by moving up 56 positions in the rankings. This arcade-style game sees players smash through ore and explore mining zones, growing their digging zones. So too has its audience grown, with 5.9m new installs meaning a shift into 36th place. October was its best month for downloads thus far.

 Most downloaded mobile games for October 2026 

 Garena’s Free Fire: Storm Arena spent its fourth consecutive month at the top of the downloads charts where it’s held a tight lead since July. It generated 25m installs this October at a rise of 15% from September.

 Constantly tailed by Roblox, the UGC platform also grew in October, up 9% in mobile installs to 22.5m.

 Hungry Studio’s Block Blast ranked third at 17.9m downloads, followed by Learnings’ 2026 hit Meowdoku at 17.3m. SmallStep Tech’s Brain Puzzle 3 rounded out the top five with 15.7m installs.

 Bus Fever Party, Paper.io 2, Rotate Rings, Ludo King and Subway Surfers completed the top 10.

 Collectively, mobile games received 3.8bn installs this October, up 4% M/M and down 5% Y/Y.

 TOP PERFORMING MOBILE GAMES PUBLISHERS

 Top grossing mobile publishers for October 2026 

 Tencent stayed on top despite an 11% fall in net player spending last month. The giant made another $295.4m, actually its worst performance of 2026 thus far, yet still no other publisher came close.

 Century Games ranked second with $146.9m, just shy of half Tencent’s revenue, while Playrix ranked third at $98.7m.

 Microfun and Roblox came close behind at $96m and $94.3m, filling out the top five.

 It’s worth noting that while Scopely ranked seventh with $89.7m, the studio would rank third if including an additional $29.8m from Scopely Explore and $8.4m from Loom Games.

 Tencent aside, many of the top publishers saw slight growth on a monthly basis.

 Top mobile publishers by downloads for October 2026 

 Voodoo, Learnings and Azur Games were last month’s top three publishers by installs, all surpassing 50m fresh downloads. Learnings and Azur Games swapped positions compared to September while Voodoo held onto first place for a second month running.

 Meanwhile, Unicorn Studio Official ranked fourth as the only other studio to surpass 50m installs last month, rising from fifth place and 44.3m downloads in September. Miniclip came fifth in October with 46.6m downloads, slightly ahead of Talking Tom maker Outfit7.

 The top five publishers all saw downloads grow compared to September, setting an encouraging course as the end of 2026 approaches.

0.headline: דוחות הרבעון השלישי חושפים: ערוצי D2C שוברים שיאי נתח שוק
key_points: בקרב מפיצות ציבוריות מובילות ב-Q3 2026, המכירות הישירות הגיעו לנתח חסר תקדים: 58% בהכנסות הסושל קזינו של DoubleDown, 47% מההזמנות ב-Stillfront ו-45.4% ב-Huuuge Games.
הכנסות ה-D2C של Playtika עלו ב-31.4% משנה לשנה ל-275.1 מיליון דולר והיוו 40.8% מסך המכירות, אך ירדו ב-4.1% רבעונית ברצף של שלושה רבעוני ירידה.
ב-MTG הגיע ה-D2C לשיא של 42% מההכנסות, כשבחטיבת המידקור Playamp הנתח עמד על 55%, לעומת 0% בחטיבת הקז'ואל Playsimple.
גוגל החלה לגבות עמלות פלטפורמה על קישורים חיצוניים באנדרואיד בארה״ב מ-1 באוקטובר 2026, מה שמצמצם את יתרון העלויות של מעקף החנויות.
0.caution: הנתונים מבוססים על מפיצות ענק ומשחקים עתירי לווייתנים כמו סושל קזינו ו-4X, ואינם משקפים כדאיות דומה עבור משחקי קז'ואל והיבריד מבוססי פרסום שבהם ה-ARPPU נמוך.
0.takeaway: יש לבחון האם ריכוז ההכנסות מלווייתנים במשחק מצדיק הקמת web shop עצמאי, תוך שקלול עמלות הקישור החיצוני החדשות של גוגל.
0.hook: כמעט מחצית מהכנסות הרכישות בתוך המשחקים של החברות הגדולות כבר לא עוברות דרך אפל וגוגל, מה שמשנה לחלוטין את מבנה המרווחים של התעשייה.
insights: ערוצי מכירה ישירה לצרכן הפכו ממנוע צמיחה שולי למנגנון העיקרי שמחזיק את שורת הרווח של מפיצות בוגרות בזמן שההכנסות הרגילות בחנויות נשחקות.
הפער התהומי בין 55% D2C במידקור של MTG ל-0% בקז'ואל של Playsimple ממחיש שמכירה ישירה עובדת רק כשיש שכבת מטא עמוקה ומועדוני VIP, ולא מתאימה לשחקני קז'ואל מזדמנים.
התגובה של גוגל עם עמלות על קישורים חיצוניים מ-1 באוקטובר מוכיחה שהפלטפורמות לא יוותרו על הנתח שלהן, והמרווח נטו של חנויות הרשת עומד להישחק.
נתוני חברות המעקב המסורתיות מציגים תמונת שוק מעוותת: ירידה בהכנסות של כותר בחנויות כבר לא מעידה על גסיסה, אלא לעיתים קרובות על מעבר של השחקנים המשלמים לרשת.
0.debate: האם ה-D2C הגיע לתקרת זכוכית של כ-50% שמעבר לה חיכוך התשלום ימנע משחקנים רגילים לעבור, או שהעמלות החדשות של הפלטפורמות יאלצו את כולם להתרגל לרכוש בדפדפן?

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: כמעט מחצית מכל הדולרים ששחקנים מוציאים במשחקים של החברות הציבוריות הגדולות כבר לא עוברים דרך אפל או גוגל.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: זה נשמע מרשים, אבל הנתון הזה מוטה לחלוטין מחברות סושל קזינו ומידקור שיש להן לווייתנים שממילא מכירים את האתר.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: הדוחות הכספיים של הרבעון השלישי של 2026 מראים שזה הפך לסטנדרט רוחבי. ב-Stillfront המכירה הישירה הגיעה ל-47% מההזמנות, וב-Huuuge Games הנתח עמד על 45.4%.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: ובכל זאת, סך ההכנסות בחלק מהחברות האלה יורד. המכירה ישירה לצרכן אולי שומר על המרווח, אבל הוא לא מייצר צמיחה אמיתית של שחקנים חדשים.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: זה בדיוק מתחבר למיקוד של התעשייה השבוע באופטימיזציה של רווחיות מול שחיקת ערוצי הרכישה. קח את Playtika: הכנסות המכירה ישירה לצרכן צמחו ב-31.4% משנה לשנה ל-275.1 מיליון דולר.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: אבל רבעונית הן ירדו ב-4.1%. זה רבעון שלישי ברציפות שהמכירות הישירות שלהם בירידה, במקביל לירידה של 14.3% בהכנסות מחנויות האפליקציות.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: נכון, אבל סמנכ״ל הכספים שלהם הבהיר שעלויות ההכנסה ירדו בעיקר בזכות הצמצום בעמלות הפלטפורמה. הם השיגו את יעד הנתח של 40.8% מוקדם מהצפוי.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: השאלה היא כמה מזה רלוונטי למי שמחזיק משחק פאזל או היבריד-קז'ואל, ולא מכונת הימורים חברתית.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: ההבדל הזה בולט מאוד בדוחות של MTG. כל החברה רשמה שיא של 42% בהכנסות ישירות, אבל חטיבת המידקור הגיעה ל-55% בעוד שחטיבת הקז'ואל Playsimple עמדה על 0% עגול.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: אפס עגול. זה אומר הכל. אם המשחק שלך מבוסס על רכישות קטנות של דולר או שניים כדי לעבור שלב, אף שחקן לא ייצא מהאפליקציה לדפדפן בשביל לחסוך עשרה סנט.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: בגלל זה Playtika השיקה את ה-web shop של Disney Solitaire רק בנובמבר. הם רוצים לבדוק אם אפשר להעביר גם שחקני קז'ואל לרשת באמצעות תוכניות נאמנות מותאמות.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: אני מנחש שהם יגלו מהר מאוד שתקרת הזכוכית בקז'ואל הרבה יותר נמוכה. בלי קהילת VIP וחיבור אישי לשחקנים, המאמץ הטכנולוגי והתפעולי פשוט נבלע בחיכוך.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: חוץ מזה, יש גורם חדש שטורף את הקלפים: גוגל התחילה לגבות עמלות על קישורים חיצוניים באנדרואיד בארה״ב מ-1 באוקטובר.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: דיברנו על החשש הזה בעבר. ברגע שהפלטפורמה לוקחת עמלה חלופית על לחיצה שמובילה לאתר, חלק משמעותי מיתרון העלויות של ה-web shop פשוט נמחק.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: מנכ״לית MTG אמרה את זה במפורש בדוח, שהכללים החדשים של גוגל מצמצמים את יתרון העלות עבור שחקנים אמריקאים.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: הפלטפורמות לא פראייריות. מצד אחד גוגל גובה עמלה על קישורים, ומצד שני Ten Square Games דיווחו שתוכנית Level Up של גוגל מציעה להם הנחה של עד 10 נקודות אחוז בעמלות בחנות.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: הם ממש נלחמים להשאיר את הטרנזקציות בפנים. ובכל זאת, אצל DoubleDown המכירות הישירות קפצו ב-170% משנה לשנה והגיעו ל-58% מסך ההכנסות.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: בסושל קזינו זה עניין של הישרדות. SciPlay דיווחה על ירידה של 12% בכלל ההכנסות בגלל חולשה בשוק, והמכירה ישירה לצרכן עלה אצלם ל-31% כדי לרכך את המכה.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: יש פה עוד זווית קריטית: הראות של התעשייה. Sensor Tower השיקה כלי להערכת הכנסות מחנויות רשת בדיוק בגלל שהכלים המסורתיים הפכו לעיוורים.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: זה עיוות עצום במחקר מתחרים. כשאתה מסתכל על נתוני הורדות והכנסות בחנויות ורואה ירידה, אתה עלול לחשוב שמשחק מסוים קורס.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: בדיוק מה שקרה עם Monopoly Go. ההכנסות בחנויות נראו בירידה, אבל ההערכות הן שכשליש מההכנסות שלו כבר מגיעות ישירות מחנות הרשת.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: אם הייתי מנהל עכשיו מוצר עם נתח הכנסות משמעותי מרכישות בתוך האפליקציה, לא הייתי רץ לבנות פלטפורמה עצמאית כמו Huuuge לפני שהייתי מנתח במדויק כמה מהשחקנים שלי הם לווייתנים אמיתיים.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: השאלה היא אם בעולם שבו הפלטפורמות גובות עמלות גם על קישורים חיצוניים, יש עדיין טעם למשחקים קטנים לנסות לפרוץ את תקרת החנויות.

1.headline: הסדר פשרה מול Google בבריטניה בגובה 338 מיליון דולר
key_points: סכום הסדר הפשרה עומד על 338 מיליון דולר (260 מיליון ליש״ט) עבור מפתחים בריטיים שמכרו ב-Google Play.
יותר מ-10,000 עסקים זכאים להגיש תביעה, והתקופה להגשת בקשות פתוחה מ-24 בנובמבר עד 24 במרץ 2027.
בית הדין לערעורים על תחרות אישר את ההסדר ב-16 בספטמבר, לאחר תביעה ייצוגית שטענה שעמלות של עד 30% ניצלו לרעה כוח שוק.
הפיצוי מחושב לפי עמלות ששולמו בין 22 באוגוסט 2018 ל-31 ביולי 2026, עם מינימום של 260 דולר למי שהכניס עד 9,750 דולר.
1.caution: הפיצוי הכספי הוא תשלום חד-פעמי רטרואקטיבי ואינו משנה את שיעור עמלות הפלטפורמה העתידיות ב-Google Play.
1.takeaway: מפתחי מובייל עם ישות בריטית שפועלים ב-Google Play חייבים לבדוק זכאות להחזר כספי באתר התביעה עד מרץ 2027.
1.hook: מפתחי מובייל בריטיים שהפרישו עד 30% עמלה ל-Google Play שמונה שנים אחורה יכולים לקבל כעת החזר מזומן מתוך קופה של 338 מיליון דולר.
insights: מנגנון ה-opt-out של התביעה הופך את היידוע לאתגר, שכן מפתחים רבים מסננים את הודעות הפיצוי כספאם.
הזרמת המזומנים הרטרואקטיבית משפרת ישירות את הרווחיות בשורה התחתונה ללא צורך בהגדלת תקציבי UA או סיכון תפעולי.
הפיצוי הכספי אינו פותר את הבעיה המבנית של עמלות החנויות או החיכוך במעבר לערוצי D2C, אלא מעניק לחברות רק אוויר לנשימה זמני.
ישנה סכנה שחברות ישתמשו בכספי הפיצוי כדי לסבסד קמפיינים לא רווחיים במקום להשקיע אותם בשימור שחקנים ובשכבות מוניטיזציה עמידות.
1.debate: האם הסטודיואים ינצלו את כספי הפיצוי כדי להשקיע במנגנוני שימור ופיתוח תשתיות רווחיות, או שישרפו אותם על קמפיינים של UA בשוק יקר?

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: מפתחי מובייל בריטיים שהפרישו עד 30% עמלה ל-Google Play שמונה שנים אחורה יכולים לקבל כעת החזר מזומן מתוך קופה של 338 מיליון דולר.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: 338 מיליון דולר נשמע כמו המון כסף, אבל מדובר על חלוקה בין 10,000 חברות זכאיות, מה שאומר שחלקן יקבלו פיצוי מינימלי של 260 דולר בלבד.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: הפיצוי המינימלי מיועד למי שהכניס עד 9,750 דולר, אבל מפתחים גדולים שילמו מיליונים בעמלות ויקבלו סכומים משמעותיים בהרבה.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: התביעה הייצוגית טענה שעמלות החנות היו מופרזות, ו-Google העדיפה לסגור בפשרה שאושרה ב-16 בספטמבר בלי להודות באחריות.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: החישוב מתבסס על עמלות ששולמו החל מ-22 באוגוסט 2018 ועד 31 ביולי 2026, כך שהטווח מכסה תקופה ארוכה מאוד.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: השחיקה בערוצי הצמיחה מקשה על כולם השבוע, אבל הזרמת מזומנים רטרואקטיבית כזו הולכת ישר לשורת הרווח.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: הבעיה היא שהתביעה התנהלה במודל opt-out, ולכן חברות רבות שקיבלו הודעה מאז שנפתח הרישום ב-24 בנובמבר בטוחות שמדובר בספאם.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: תאריך היעד להגשת בקשה הוא 24 במרץ 2027, כך שיש זמן, אבל מי שלא יבדוק אקטיבית פשוט ישאיר את הכסף על השולחן.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: אם הייתי מנהלת סטודיו למשחקי פאזל או היבריד-קז'ואל בבריטניה, הייתי נכנסת כבר היום לאתר הרשמי לבדוק את ההקצאה הזמנית.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: השאלה היא מה עושים עם הכסף. סטודיו שיקבל מאה אלף דולר עלול לסבסד קמפיינים כושלים במקום להשקיע בשימור שחקנים.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: או שהוא ינצל את הרווח הנקי כדי לחזק אירועים חיים ומנגנוני מוניטיזציה למשתמשים קיימים, בדיוק בתקופה שבה רכישת שחקנים חדשים יקרה מדי.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: החזר חד-פעמי גם לא פותר את החיכוך סביב חנויות חיצוניות ועמלות חלופיות של 27% שראינו במאבקים הקודמים מול הפלטפורמות.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: ב-MobileGamer.biz גם מציינים שההסדר הזה נפרד לחלוטין מתביעת הצרכנים שעדיין מתנהלת בבית הדין, כך שהלחץ המשפטי יימשך.

script.speaker: Yoni
script.text: בסופו של דבר החלוקה בפועל תאושר רק לאחר שבית הדין יסקור את הבקשות בתום התקופה, אז המזומנים לא יגיעו מחר בבוקר.

script.speaker: Dana
script.text: הכל תלוי בשאלה אם המפתחים יראו בזה אוויר לנשימה לבניית מודלים יציבים יותר או רק כיסוי להפסדים הקיימים.
